## Solution

### Evaluating $I = \int_0^\infty x^{1/2} e^{-x^3}\,dx$

Use the substitution $t = x^3$, so $x = t^{1/3}$ and $dx = \tfrac{1}{3} t^{-2/3}\,dt$. The limits are unchanged ($x=0 \Rightarrow t=0$, $x\to\infty \Rightarrow t\to\infty$). Also $x^{1/2} = t^{1/6}$. Hence

$$
I = \int_0^\infty t^{1/6} e^{-t} \cdot \tfrac{1}{3} t^{-2/3}\,dt = \frac{1}{3}\int_0^\infty t^{1/6 - 2/3} e^{-t}\,dt = \frac{1}{3}\int_0^\infty t^{-1/2} e^{-t}\,dt.
$$

Since $t^{-1/2} = t^{1/2 - 1}$, the remaining integral is $\Gamma\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right) = \sqrt{\pi}$. Therefore

$$
\boxed{I = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{3}}.
$$

### Evaluating $J = \int_0^1 x^{-2/3}(1-x)^{-1/3}\,dx$

This is the Euler Beta integral $B(a,b) = \int_0^1 x^{a-1}(1-x)^{b-1}\,dx = \frac{\Gamma(a)\Gamma(b)}{\Gamma(a+b)}$, with

$$
a - 1 = -\tfrac{2}{3} \;\Rightarrow\; a = \tfrac{1}{3}, \qquad b - 1 = -\tfrac{1}{3} \;\Rightarrow\; b = \tfrac{2}{3}.
$$

Thus

$$
J = B\!\left(\tfrac{1}{3}, \tfrac{2}{3}\right) = \frac{\Gamma(\tfrac{1}{3})\,\Gamma(\tfrac{2}{3})}{\Gamma(1)} = \Gamma\!\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)\Gamma\!\left(\tfrac{2}{3}\right).
$$

Apply the reflection formula $\Gamma(z)\Gamma(1-z) = \dfrac{\pi}{\sin(\pi z)}$ with $z = \tfrac{1}{3}$ (so $1-z = \tfrac{2}{3}$):

$$
\Gamma\!\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)\Gamma\!\left(\tfrac{2}{3}\right) = \frac{\pi}{\sin(\pi/3)} = \frac{\pi}{\sqrt{3}/2} = \frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{3}}.
$$

Therefore

$$
\boxed{J = \frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{3}}}.
$$

### The ratio $\dfrac{J}{I}$

$$
\frac{J}{I} = \frac{\,2\pi/\sqrt{3}\,}{\,\sqrt{\pi}/3\,} = \frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{3}} \cdot \frac{3}{\sqrt{\pi}} = \frac{6\pi}{\sqrt{3}\,\sqrt{\pi}} = \frac{6\pi}{\sqrt{3\pi}}.
$$

Rationalizing by multiplying numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{3\pi}$:

$$
\frac{J}{I} = \frac{6\pi\sqrt{3\pi}}{3\pi} = \frac{6\sqrt{3\pi}}{3} = 2\sqrt{3\pi}.
$$

Hence

$$
\boxed{\dfrac{J}{I} = 2\sqrt{3\pi}}.
$$
